chunks.title: [CLO Official Tutorial Video with Chinese Subtitles] Detail Series p08 8. Adding Padding Effects
chunks.content: ## Opening Project Files and Preparing the Workspace This section explains how to access and prepare the necessary project files in CLO for adding padding effects, focusing on file navigation and initial tool selection. - Open the **Project Files** folder by double-clicking in the window. - Navigate to **C.Details** and locate the **G.Adding Paddings** file. - Double-click the **Jacket Padding** file or drag it into either the 3D or 2D window to load it. - In the 2D toolbar, select the **Edit Pattern** tool (often referred to as Edit Files). - Right-click on the bottom lines of the front and back pattern pieces to prepare for editing inputs. ## Drawing and Editing Internal Lines on the Sleeve This section covers how to create and manipulate internal lines on the sleeve pattern to define padding areas using CLO’s Line Tool and Edit Pattern tool. - In the Inputs panel, select the **Line Tool**. - Draw a right-angle line on the sleeve piece in the 2D window. - Use the **Edit Pattern** tool to select the newly created line. - Press **Ctrl-C** to copy the line and then **Ctrl-V** to paste it. - Move the copied line with the mouse; right-click to open the menu, enter the desired number for duplication, then confirm with **OK**. - Newly created lines will be highlighted in yellow, indicating they are selected. - With the **Edit Pattern** tool, click to confirm selections. - Right-click on a selected internal line and choose the option to convert or modify it as needed. - In the 2D toolbar, select the fifth tool (likely a specific editing or transformation tool) and click to activate. - Ensure all internal lines are within the selected frame using the **Edit Pattern** tool. - Copy internal lines with **Ctrl-C** and paste with **Ctrl-R**. - The outline of the copied internal line follows the mouse; right-click on the sleeve and select the appropriate menu option to finalize placement. - On the newly added internal line, right-click and select the necessary function to confirm or adjust the line. ## Applying Fabric and Adjusting Pressure Settings This section details how to assign fabric properties and adjust pressure settings on pattern layers to simulate padding effects realistically. - Double-click to open the **FABRIK** folder. - Select the **Nylon Featherweight** fabric file and drag it into the **FABRIK 1** object window. - Press the **FABRIK** button to ensure the fabric is applied to the correct object window. - In the 2D window, select the **outer layer** of the shell pattern and set the **pressure** value to **20** to simulate fabric tension. - Then select the **inner layer** of the shell pattern for further adjustments (details of inner layer settings were incomplete but imply further pressure or fabric settings). - Open the 3D model view and apply the fabric and pressure settings to visualize the padding effect on the jacket.
